en.title: How To Play
en.description: Dorios’ Basics adds tools and workstations for making early resources from common blocks. Dig up fragments with a hammer, sift blocks for materials and make water or lava as your world expands.

pages.label: How To Play
pages.title: Dorios' Basics
pages.intro: Dorios’ Basics adds tools and workstations for making early resources from common blocks. Dig up fragments with a hammer, sift blocks for materials and make water or lava as your world expands.

sections.title: Pebbles
paragraphs: Sneak and interact with grass or dirt while holding a hammer to search for stone pebbles, gravel fragments, dirt, sand and other materials. Mud can yield Mud Balls. Red Sand and Terracotta can yield Red Sand Handfuls. Use the crafting recipes for the fragments you collect to turn them into full blocks.

sections.title: Hammers
paragraphs: Mine the input block directly with a hammer to convert it. A wooden hammer is enough to start the Cobblestone → Gravel → Dirt → Sand chain.

sections.title: Flint Knife
paragraphs: Arrange 3 gravel in an L to craft flint. Place the flint diagonally above a stick to make the Flint Knife. Break leaves with it for a chance to get Plant Fiber, then craft four fibers in a 2×2 square to make a string.

sections.title: Mortar — Getting Water
paragraphs: Craft a Mortar with a Stone Pebble between two cobblestone and another cobblestone below it. At a crafting table, put 2 saplings in a row, with the Mortar and a Glass Bottle on the row underneath. This gives you a Water Bottle and returns the Mortar.

sections.title: Sieve
steps: Use a mesh on the Sieve to equip it.
Hold a siftable block, such as gravel, and interact with the Sieve to add it.
Keep interacting to sift the block and collect the results. The input block and mesh tier determine what can drop.
To remove the mesh, sneak and interact with an empty hand.
paragraphs: An interaction also works on sieves in a 5×5 square centered on the sieve you use, at the same height. Bring enough blocks to fill the whole group.

sections.title: Crucible
paragraphs: Place a heat source directly under the Crucible and add 4 cobblestone. Each cobblestone melts into a quarter bucket of lava. When it is full, use an empty bucket to collect the lava or a Water Bucket to turn it into obsidian.

rows: Fire, Campfire, Magma Block, Big Torch
Soul Fire, Soul Torch, Soul Campfire

sections.title: Sink
paragraphs: The Sink provides an infinite source of water for compatible UtilityCraft fluid setups.

en.title: How To Play
en.description: Turn resources you already have into crops you can harvest repeatedly. Start with a Base Seed, craft the seed for your chosen resource and plant it on the soil that matches its tier.

pages.label: How To Play
pages.title: Bountiful Crops
pages.intro: Turn resources you already have into crops you can harvest repeatedly. Start with a Base Seed, craft the seed for your chosen resource and plant it on the soil that matches its tier.

rows: Coal, Copper, Dyes, Glass, Gunpowder, Iron, Leather, Prismarine Crystals, Prismarine Shards, Water, Wool
Ghast Tear, Glowstone, Gold, Honey, Lapis, Lava, Quartz, Redstone, Resin, Slime
Amethyst, Blaze, Diamond, Emerald, Ender Pearl, Obsidian
Netherite, Nether Star, Shulker, Totem, Wither

sections.title: Crafting the Base Seed
paragraphs: At a crafting table, put 1 wheat seed in the center, 4 bone meal on the sides and 4 glass in the corners. Use the Base Seed with the ingredients for the crop you want. To make Iron Seeds, for example, put a Base Seed in the center and surround it with 8 iron ingots.

sections.title: Resource Drops
paragraphs: Interact with a mature plant to collect its resources and reset it to the first growth stage. Breaking a mature plant also returns the seed you need to replant it.

When you interact with the crop using a Fortune tool, the harvest amount is multiplied by 1.2×, 1.4× or 1.6× for Fortune I, II or III, with fractional amounts rounded by chance. You can craft shards, fragments and nuggets into their full resources.

headers: Drops per mature harvest before Fortune

sections.title: Special Crops
paragraphs: Water, Lava and Honey produce balls of their respective liquids. Combine Water and Lava Balls to craft Obsidian, or use Honey Balls in the recipes for Honey Bottles and Honey Blocks.

sections.title: Accelerating Growth
paragraphs: Put an Accelerator Clock on a Pedestal at the same height as your crops. It attempts to advance crops in a 9×9 area centered on the Pedestal. The Diamond and Nether Star clocks have a higher chance of advancing each crop than the standard clock. Interact with the Pedestal again to take the clock back.

sections.title: Integration with UtilityCraft
paragraphs: The addon registers its crop seeds with UtilityCraft’s plant system, so a compatible Bonsai Pot can grow them in a compact setup.

en.title: How To Play
en.description: Craft an ore sapling from materials you already have, then grow it to harvest more of that resource. Breaking the leaves can return saplings for replanting.

pages.label: How To Play
pages.title: Bountiful Trees
pages.intro: Craft an ore sapling from materials you already have, then grow it to harvest more of that resource. Breaking the leaves can return saplings for replanting.

sections.title: Crafting Ore Saplings
paragraphs: Place an oak sapling in the center of the crafting table. Use the layout in your sapling’s recipe group.
For example, a Redstone Sapling takes four blocks of redstone and four redstone dust. A Copper Sapling takes one block of copper and seven copper ingots.

rows: Copper, Iron, Gold, Diamond, Emerald, Netherite
Put one storage block directly below the sapling. Fill the other seven spaces with the loose material.
Put storage blocks on the four sides. Fill the four corners with the loose material.

sections.title: Growth and Harvest
paragraphs: Plant the sapling with room for its canopy to spread up to two blocks each way. It can grow naturally on a random tick. Each application of bone meal gives it a 20% chance to grow immediately.

Harvest the ore logs with an axe or pickaxe. Each eligible log gives its corresponding resource, and Fortune can add more. The oak sapling is the starting ingredient for the recipe. The ore logs are the source of the materials below.
Break the leaves to try for sticks or a matching ore sapling.

sections.title: UtilityCraft Compatibility
paragraphs: Bountiful Trees registers saplings with UtilityCraft’s plant system for compatible Bonsai Pots. The Bonsai harvest tables can use different forms of a resource, such as Diamond Shards and Netherite Nuggets.

en.title: How To Play
en.description: Use the Training Dummy to measure how hard a hit lands and how much damage your attack rhythm delivers. Placing the Dummy Block spawns a stationary target in front of you.

pages.label: How To Play
pages.title: Training Dummy
pages.intro: Use the Training Dummy to measure how hard a hit lands and how much damage your attack rhythm delivers. Placing the Dummy Block spawns a stationary target in front of you.

sections.title: Crafting and Placement
paragraphs: At a crafting table, put 1 hay bale above the middle of a row of 3 logs. Place the resulting Dummy Block where you can stand at your usual attack distance.

sections.title: Reading Damage

rows: The damage Bedrock reported for one hit credited to a player.
Total damage from player hits in the last 20 game ticks, about one second at normal tick speed.

paragraphs: Both readings update automatically. Wait for the DPS display to return to zero before trying another weapon or loadout. If a projectile or scripted ability registers no reading, check whether Bedrock credits the hit to the player.

en.title: How To Play
en.description: Redstone Lamps Plus brings the lamp designs of LicitLettuce’s Java Edition project to Minecraft Bedrock. Use them for switchable lighting in builds with redstone wiring.

pages.label: How To Play
pages.title: Redstone Lamps Plus
pages.intro: Redstone Lamps Plus brings the lamp designs of LicitLettuce’s Java Edition project to Minecraft Bedrock. Use them for switchable lighting in builds with redstone wiring.

sections.title: How It Works
steps: Place a lamp and connect a redstone source. A lever next to the lamp is a simple way to test it.
Power the lamp to light it.
Break or switch off the signal to put the lamp out.
paragraphs: For a timed pulse, use a button. For a lamp that stays on until you switch it off, use a lever or a redstone torch circuit.

sections.title: Visual Enhancements
paragraphs: The pack supports both Vibrant Visuals and RTX. When your device supports one of these modes, enable it in Minecraft’s video settings to see the corresponding lighting effects. The redstone circuit controls when the lamp turns on in every graphics mode.

sections.title: Compatibility
paragraphs: Use the behavior and resource packs from the same addon release. Check the version listed for the file you plan to import. Redstone Lamps Plus downloads

sections.title: Credits
paragraphs: Original Java Edition lamp designs by LicitLettuce. Bedrock adaptation by Dorios Studios.

en.title: How To Play
en.description: Build an Effect Pillar to apply a status effect around a base, mine or mob farm. You choose the effect, its level and its range independently.

pages.label: How To Play
pages.title: Effect Pillars
pages.intro: Build an Effect Pillar to apply a status effect around a base, mine or mob farm. You choose the effect, its level and its range independently.

sections.title: Pillar Components
paragraphs: Build the stack from the bottom up. Place the Base Stone as the foundation, then the Level block, then the Range block, and finally the Effect block. The effect block checks the two blocks immediately beneath it. Interact with the effect block to turn it on or off.

sections.title: Effect Beacons

rows: Absorption, Conduit Power, Fire Resistance, Haste, Health Boost, Hero of the Village, Invisibility, Jump Boost, Night Vision, Regeneration, Resistance, Saturation, Slow Falling, Speed, Strength and Water Breathing
Area Damage, Poison, Slowness, Weakness and Wither

paragraphs: Use Haste above a mine or Water Breathing over an underwater build. For Levitation, hold sneak while within range to rise.

sections.title: Base Stone
paragraphs: Put one block of coal in the center of a crafting grid, four blackstone on the sides, and four cobbled deepslate in the corners.

sections.title: Guide Book
paragraphs: Combine 1 paper with 1 Base Stone at a crafting table to make the Effect Pillars guide book. Open it in-game to look up the individual effect recipes.

en.title: How To Play
en.description: The Copper Cobblestone Generator is the first tier. It produces one cobblestone every four seconds and sends its output directly into an adjacent container. Each of the five upgrades uses the previous generator as an ingredient.

pages.label: How To Play
pages.title: Cobblestone Generators
pages.intro: The Copper Cobblestone Generator is the first tier. It produces one cobblestone every four seconds and sends its output directly into an adjacent container. Each of the five upgrades uses the previous generator as an ingredient.

sections.title: Crafting the Generator
paragraphs: Make the copper tier at a crafting table with 4 copper ingots, 2 obsidian, 1 glass, 1 water bucket and 1 lava bucket. The recipe returns two empty buckets.
For an upgrade, put the previous generator in the center and surround it with eight of the material shown below.

sections.title: Generator Tiers
paragraphs: These rates describe the generator while it is ticking and has space to store or deliver its output.

sections.title: How It Works
paragraphs: Place a chest or barrel against the face with the output port. If the container is missing or runs out of room, the generator stores up to 64 cobblestone. Interact with an empty main hand to collect the stored cobblestone, or free space in the connected container so the generator can transfer it on its next cycle.

en.title: How To Play
en.description: Compressy combines stacks of common materials into blocks or bundles that you can unpack later. These recipes come from version 1.0.3.

pages.label: How To Play
pages.title: Compressy
pages.intro: Compressy combines stacks of common materials into blocks or bundles that you can unpack later. These recipes come from version 1.0.3.

sections.title: Compress and unpack
paragraphs: Fill a crafting table’s 3×3 grid with one block or item per slot to make one compressed result. Put a single compressed result back in the crafting grid to recover the nine inputs. Paper is the exception: use six sheets in two complete rows to make one Ream of Paper, which unpacks into six sheets.

sections.title: Block compression tiers
paragraphs: Each level uses nine blocks of the preceding level. Most materials stop at tier 4. Cobblestone continues through tier 9. Nether Stars have a separate first step: nine stars make one Nether Star Block, and that block then has four compression tiers. Its tier 4 represents 59,049 stars.

sections.title: Supported materials

rows: Andesite, basalt, blackstone, calcite, cobbled deepslate, cobblestone, crying obsidian, deepslate, diorite, dripstone block, end stone, granite, netherrack, obsidian, stone and tuff
Clay, dirt, glass, gravel, honey block, moss block, mud, red sand, sand, slime block, soul sand and soul soil
Amethyst, coal, copper, diamond, emerald, gold, iron, lapis lazuli, netherite, quartz, raw copper, raw gold, raw iron, redstone and Nether Star
Acacia, birch, cherry, dark oak, jungle, mangrove, oak, pale oak and spruce wood, plus bamboo block, crimson hyphae and warped hyphae
All 16 dyes, beetroot seeds, cocoa beans, melon seeds, pitcher pod, pumpkin seeds, torchflower seeds and wheat seeds
Blaze powder and rods, breeze rods, cookies, feathers, ghast tears, glow ink sacs, glowstone dust, gunpowder, ink sacs, paper, spider eyes, fermented spider eyes, sticks, string and sugar

paragraphs: Compressy shares item and block identifiers with UtilityCraft. Use Compressy as a standalone alternative in worlds where you want only the compression recipes.

pt-BR.description: Compressy transforma pilhas de materiais comuns em blocos ou pacotes que você pode descompactar depois. Estas receitas correspondem à versão 1.0.3.

pages.label: How To Play
pages.title: Compressy
pages.intro: Compressy transforma pilhas de materiais comuns em blocos ou pacotes que você pode descompactar depois. Estas receitas correspondem à versão 1.0.3.

sections.title: Compactar e descompactar
paragraphs: Preencha a grade 3×3 da bancada com uma unidade do material por espaço para obter um resultado compactado. Coloque um resultado compactado na grade para recuperar as nove unidades originais. O papel é a exceção: seis folhas em duas linhas completas formam uma resma, que devolve seis folhas.

sections.title: Níveis de compactação
paragraphs: Cada nível usa nove blocos do nível anterior. A maioria dos materiais chega ao nível 4. O pedregulho vai até o nível 9. Para estrelas do Nether há uma etapa inicial: nove estrelas formam um Bloco de Estrela do Nether, que pode ser compactado em quatro níveis. O nível 4 equivale a 59.049 estrelas.

sections.title: Materiais aceitos

rows: Andesito, basalto, calcita, diorito, granito, netherrack, obsidiana, obsidiana chorona, pedra, bloco de espeleotema, pedra do End, pedra-negra, pedregulho, pedregulho de ardósia, ardósia e tufo
Argila, areia, areia das almas, areia vermelha, bloco de mel, bloco de limo, bloco de musgo, cascalho, lama, solo das almas, terra e vidro
Ametista, carvão, cobre, diamante, esmeralda, ferro, lápis-lazúli, netherita, ouro, quartzo, redstone, cobre bruto, ferro bruto, ouro bruto e Estrela do Nether
Acácia, bétula, carvalho, carvalho escuro, carvalho pálido, cerejeira, floresta, mangue e pinheiro, além de bloco de bambu e hifas carmesim e distorcidas
Todos os 16 corantes, grãos de cacau, vagem de planta-jarro e sementes de abóbora, beterraba, flor-tocha, melancia e trigo

Açúcar, biscoito, graveto, lágrima de ghast, linha, olho de aranha, olho de aranha fermentado, papel, pena, pólvora, pó de blaze, pó de pedra luminosa, bolsa de tinta, bolsa de tinta brilhante, vara de blaze e vara de breeze

paragraphs: Compressy compartilha identificadores de itens e blocos com UtilityCraft. Use Compressy separadamente em mundos onde deseja apenas as receitas de compactação.

es-MX.title: How To Play
es-MX.description: Compressy reúne materiales comunes en bloques o paquetes que puedes descomprimir después. Estas recetas corresponden a la versión 1.0.3.

pages.label: How To Play
pages.title: Compressy
pages.intro: Compressy reúne materiales comunes en bloques o paquetes que puedes descomprimir después. Estas recetas corresponden a la versión 1.0.3.

sections.title: Comprimir y descomprimir
paragraphs: Llena la cuadrícula 3×3 de la mesa de trabajo con una unidad del material en cada casilla para obtener un resultado comprimido. Pon un resultado comprimido en la cuadrícula para recuperar las nueve unidades. El papel es la excepción: coloca seis hojas en dos filas completas para fabricar una resma, que devuelve seis hojas.

sections.title: Niveles de compresión
paragraphs: Cada nivel usa nueve bloques del nivel anterior. La mayoría de los materiales llega al nivel 4. El adoquín llega al nivel 9. Las estrellas del Nether tienen un paso inicial: nueve estrellas forman un bloque de estrella del Nether, que tiene cuatro niveles de compresión. Su nivel 4 equivale a 59,049 estrellas.

Acacia, abedul, cerezo, jungla, mangle, roble, roble oscuro, roble pálido y abeto, además de bloque de bambú e hifas carmesí y distorsionadas
Los 16 tintes, granos de cacao, vaina de planta odre y semillas de calabaza, flor antorcha, remolacha, sandía y trigo

Azúcar, galleta, hilo, lágrima de ghast, ojo de araña, ojo de araña fermentado, palo, papel, pluma, polvo de blaze, polvo de piedra luminosa, pólvora, saco de tinta, saco de tinta brillante, vara de blaze y vara de brisa

paragraphs: Compressy comparte identificadores de bloques y objetos con UtilityCraft. Usa Compressy por separado en mundos donde solo quieras las recetas de compresión.

en.title: How To Play
en.description: A Paxel combines a pickaxe, axe and shovel. An AIOT (All-In-One Tool) adds the sword and hoe functions, including a 3×3 farming action. This guide uses the item definitions from version 1.0.5.

pages.label: How To Play
pages.title: Paxels & AIOTs
pages.intro: A Paxel combines a pickaxe, axe and shovel. An AIOT (All-In-One Tool) adds the sword and hoe functions, including a 3×3 farming action. This guide uses the item definitions from version 1.0.5.

sections.title: Recipes

rows: 1 pickaxe, 1 shovel and 1 axe of the same material, plus 4 string and 2 sticks
1 Paxel, 1 sword and 1 hoe of the same material, plus 3 units of that material, 2 string and 1 stick
Upgrade the corresponding diamond tool with 1 Netherite Upgrade smithing template and 1 netherite ingot at a smithing table

paragraphs: For a wooden AIOT, use planks as the extra material. Use cobblestone for stone tools and ingots for copper, iron and gold. Diamond requires three diamonds.

sections.title: Crafting grid
paragraphs: Slots run left to right, from the top row to the bottom row.

sections.title: Tool stats by material
paragraphs: Mining speed shows the range across configured block rules. The actual time to break a block also depends on the block and conditions. Both tool families use the Bedrock axe enchantment slot.

sections.title: Use an AIOT on a block
bullets: Use while standing to till eligible soil and harvest supported crops in a 3×3 area.
Use while sneaking to turn eligible soil into dirt paths in a 3×3 area.
Using the tool also clears snow and snow layers in the 3×3 area at the targeted height and one block above. You can use this action while standing or sneaking.

pt-BR.title: How To Play
pt-BR.description: O Paxel combina picareta, machado e pá. A AIOT reúne essas ferramentas com espada e enxada e oferece uma ação de cultivo em área 3×3. Este guia usa as definições da versão 1.0.5.

pages.label: How To Play
pages.title: Paxels & AIOTs
pages.intro: O Paxel combina picareta, machado e pá. A AIOT reúne essas ferramentas com espada e enxada e oferece uma ação de cultivo em área 3×3. Este guia usa as definições da versão 1.0.5.

sections.title: Receitas

rows: 1 picareta, 1 pá e 1 machado do mesmo material, mais 4 linhas e 2 gravetos
1 Paxel, 1 espada e 1 enxada do mesmo material, mais 3 unidades daquele material, 2 linhas e 1 graveto
Na bancada de ferraria, use a ferramenta de diamante correspondente, 1 molde de melhoria de netherita e 1 barra de netherita

paragraphs: Para uma AIOT de madeira, o material extra são tábuas. Para pedra, use pedregulho. Para cobre, ferro e ouro, use barras. Para diamante, use três diamantes.

sections.title: Grade de fabricação
paragraphs: Leia os espaços da esquerda para a direita, de cima para baixo.

sections.title: Estatísticas por material
paragraphs: A velocidade de mineração mostra o intervalo das regras configuradas para os blocos. O tempo para quebrar um bloco também depende do bloco e das condições. As duas famílias usam o tipo de encantamento de machado do Bedrock.

sections.title: Usar uma AIOT em um bloco
bullets: Use em pé para arar os solos aceitos e colher os cultivos compatíveis em uma área 3×3.
Use agachado para criar caminhos de terra nos solos aceitos em uma área 3×3.
A ferramenta também remove neve e camadas de neve na área 3×3, na altura do bloco alvo e um bloco acima. Essa ação funciona em pé ou agachado.

es-MX.title: How To Play
es-MX.description: Un Paxel combina un pico, un hacha y una pala. Una AIOT añade las funciones de la espada y la azada, con una acción de cultivo en un área de 3×3. Esta guía usa las definiciones de la versión 1.0.5.

pages.label: How To Play
pages.title: Paxels & AIOTs
pages.intro: Un Paxel combina un pico, un hacha y una pala. Una AIOT añade las funciones de la espada y la azada, con una acción de cultivo en un área de 3×3. Esta guía usa las definiciones de la versión 1.0.5.

sections.title: Recetas

rows: 1 pico, 1 pala y 1 hacha del mismo material, más 4 hilos y 2 palos
1 Paxel, 1 espada y 1 azada del mismo material, más 3 unidades de ese material, 2 hilos y 1 palo
En la mesa de herrería, usa la herramienta de diamante correspondiente, 1 plantilla de mejora de netherita y 1 lingote de netherita

paragraphs: Usa tablas para una AIOT de madera, adoquín para piedra y lingotes para cobre, hierro y oro. Para diamante, usa tres diamantes.

sections.title: Cuadrícula de fabricación
paragraphs: Lee las casillas de izquierda a derecha, de arriba abajo.

sections.title: Estadísticas por material
paragraphs: La velocidad de minado muestra el intervalo de las reglas configuradas para los bloques. El tiempo para romper un bloque también depende del bloque y de las condiciones. Ambas familias usan el tipo de encantamiento de hacha de Bedrock.

sections.title: Usar una AIOT en un bloque
bullets: Úsala de pie para arar los suelos compatibles y cosechar los cultivos compatibles en un área de 3×3.
Úsala agachado para crear caminos en los suelos compatibles en un área de 3×3.
La herramienta también quita nieve y capas de nieve en el área de 3×3 a la altura del bloque seleccionado y un bloque por encima. Esta acción funciona de pie o agachado.

en.title: How To Play
en.description: Sneak and break an eligible block to mine matching blocks together. Use the settings book to select a shape, a block limit, and which blocks are eligible.

pages.label: How To Play
pages.title: Set up vein mining
pages.intro: Sneak and break an eligible block to mine matching blocks together. Use the settings book to select a shape, a block limit, and which blocks are eligible.

sections.title: Available Commands
code:
excavateadd              – Adds a block to your personal excavate whitelist.
excavateblacklistadd     – Adds a block to the global blacklist. (Admin only)
excavateblacklistremove  – Removes a block from the global blacklist. (Admin only)
excavatedefaultadd       – Adds a block to the global default list. (Admin only)
excavatedefaultremove    – Removes a block from the global default list. (Admin only)
excavatelimit            – Sets your personal block limit for excavate.
excavateopenmenu         – Opens your personal excavate configuration menu.
excavateremove           – Removes a block from your personal excavate whitelist.
excavateshape            – Changes your current excavate shape or pattern.
excavatetoggle           – Toggles your excavate ability on or off.

sections.title: Fully Configurable
paragraphs: Every player can personalize their excavation behavior using the in-game menu or commands.You can choose what blocks are excavatable, how far the ability reaches, and which shape defines your digging pattern.

sections.title: Available Shapes
code:
Line          – Mines straight forward, ideal for quick tunnels.
Small Tunnel  – Perfect 1×2 tunnels for easy exploration.
Large Tunnel  – Instantly clears a 3×3 path.
Vein          – Classic ore or tree vein mining mode (shapeless).

sections.title: Configuration Menu
paragraphs: The configuration menu allows you to:
Everything is designed for simplicity — quick setup, no command knowledge required.
bullets: Add or remove blocks from your personal whitelist
Change your current Shape Mode
Adjust your Block Limit
Enable or disable excavation on demand

sections.title: Notes
bullets: Works seamlessly with achievements enabled worlds.
Optimized to minimize lag on large operations.

en.title: How To Play
en.description: Plant a sapling or seed in a Bonsai Pot and harvest its drops. The plant and soil determine the growth time and possible resources.

pages.label: How To Play
pages.title: Bountiful Bonsais – Introduction
pages.intro: Plant a sapling or seed in a Bonsai Pot and harvest its drops. The plant and soil determine the growth time and possible resources.

sections.title: Overview
bullets: 🌳 Grow trees and crops automatically
🪴 Use different soils to adjust growth time
⚙️ Integrate with UtilityCraft containers for full automation
💎 Discover 26 unique bonsai types covering every tree and crop from Minecraft
paragraphs: Each bonsai grows over time and drops its resources directly into the container below (such as a chest or barrel).No hoppers are required — making early automation simple and efficient.

sections.title: Getting Started
paragraphs: To start using bonsais, you’ll need to craft a Bonsai Pot, place it over a container, and plant a sapling or seed along with a compatible soil.Once placed, it will automatically begin producing items every growth cycle.

pages.label: Crafting and Setup
pages.title: Crafting and Setup
pages.intro: Before your bonsai can start producing resources, you’ll first need to craft a Bonsai Pot and understand how it works.

sections.title: Crafting the Bonsai Pot
paragraphs: The Bonsai Pot is the core block of the addon.It acts as the growing platform where all bonsais are planted.
Recipe:
Once crafted, it’s ready to be placed anywhere.
bullets: 3 × Stone Slabs
1 × Hopper
2 × Planks

sections.title: Placing and Using the Bonsai
paragraphs: Place your bonsai on top of a container, such as a Chest or Barrel.This allows it to automatically store all generated items — no hopper is required.
Each bonsai collects its drops directly in the block beneath it.You can use any container that supports item storage, including UtilityCraft blocks.

sections.title: Soil Setup
paragraphs: Every bonsai requires a soil to grow.Different soils affect growth speed and compatibility with plants.

sections.title: Growth Speed Modifiers
paragraphs: Using a hoe on soil increases growth speed — except on special soils from UtilityCraft or Bountiful Crops, which already have unique properties.

sections.title: Compatible Soils and Plants
paragraphs: The base growth time for any bonsai is 60 seconds, reduced further by certain soils and upgrades.

sections.title: Planting a Tree
paragraphs: Once you’ve added soil, take a sapling or seed and interact with the bonsai to plant it.If placed correctly, a miniature version of the plant will appear.
Your bonsai will now begin to grow and automatically produce resources.
💡 Tip: You don’t need a hopper below the bonsai.It will automatically transfer items to the container beneath it.

sections.title: Removing or Resetting
paragraphs: You can remove:
bullets: Only the bonsai using shears (keeps the soil)
Both bonsai and soil by sneaking and breaking it with your hand

sections.title: Next Steps
paragraphs: Now that your bonsai is producing items, it’s time to understand how growth mechanics and loot work —including drop rates, special soils, and how to fully automate your setup.

pages.label: Growth & Drops
pages.title: Growth & Drops
pages.intro: Every bonsai follows a simple cycle: grow → harvest → repeat. The type of soil, the plant, and certain modifiers directly affect the growth speed and loot outcome.

sections.title: Growth Time
paragraphs: By default, each bonsai takes 60 seconds to complete a full growth cycle.However, this time can be reduced with better soils or certain actions.
Some soils can multiply the output or cut the growth time in half, depending on their tier.

sections.title: Special Soils
paragraphs: When combined with UtilityCraft or Bountiful Crops, you gain access to special soils that greatly boost bonsai performance.These soils cannot be hoed and each offers unique benefits.
💡 Tip: Higher-tier soils not only shorten growth time,but also multiply the amount of drops produced by your bonsais.

sections.title: Drop Mechanics
paragraphs: Each bonsai generates resources once its growth cycle completes.The type and amount of loot depend on the bonsai type, soil, and RNG.

All drops are automatically inserted into the container below the bonsai (Barrel, Chest, or compatible block).You can chain multiple containers or connect them with UtilityCraft hoppers or uppers for transport.

sections.title: Multipliers & Efficiency
paragraphs: Every bonsai calculates its total output like this:
Base Drops × Soil Multiplier
For example:
bullets: A Dirt Bonsai might yield 6–10 logs.
The same bonsai on Blue Soil could yield up to 20.
On Black Soil, it can reach 40 or more per cycle.
